message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Tamar Valley Homes' repairs policy (October 2026). Report repairs any time by phone, online or by email; emergencies by phone only. Emergencies (immediate danger, gas leaks, no electricity, flooding, insecure external doors) are attended within 4 hours and made safe within 24. Urgent repairs, such as the only toilet blocked or no heating between October and April, are done within 3 working days. Routine jobs like dripping taps, sticking doors and loose tiles are done within 10 working days. The landlord looks after the structure and exterior, the water, gas, electricity, heating and sanitation installations it provided, communal areas, and boundary fences on public roads, and services all gas appliances in the home, including cookers, with an annual safety check. Tenants handle decoration, bulbs, plugs and fuses, sinks blocked through misuse, and fences between neighbours' gardens (unless installed by the landlord in the last 5 years). If you are locked out or lose your keys, Tamar Valley will change the locks free of charge. Access must be given at reasonable times with 24 hours' notice; two missed appointments can close the request. Missed landlord appointments earn £15 rent credit. Tenant-caused damage is recharged. Tenants aged 75+ or disabled with no help at home can ask for help with minor jobs.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
TAMAR VALLEY HOMES — REPAIRS AND MAINTENANCE POLICY FOR TENANTS (Summary version, October 2026)

1. Reporting repairs. Repairs can be reported 24 hours a day by telephone (0345 600 2210), online through My Account, or by email. Emergency repairs must be reported by telephone.

2. Repair categories and target times. • Emergency: where there is an immediate risk to health, safety or security, or serious damage to the property (for example, a gas leak, total loss of electricity, flooding, or an external door that cannot be secured). We will attend within 4 hours and make safe within 24 hours. A follow-on repair may be needed. • Urgent: problems that seriously affect comfort or convenience, such as a blocked toilet where there is no other toilet, or loss of heating between 1 October and 30 April. We will complete the repair within 3 working days. • Routine: all other repairs, such as dripping taps, sticking doors or loose floor tiles. We will complete the repair within 20 working days. • Planned: larger works such as kitchen and bathroom replacement, carried out under our planned programme.

3. Our responsibilities. We are responsible for the structure and exterior of your home; installations for water, gas, electricity, heating and sanitation that we provided; communal areas; and boundary walls and fences that front a public road. We arrange the annual gas safety check of all gas appliances that we installed, such as boilers and fires.

4. Your responsibilities. Tenants are responsible for: internal decoration; replacing light bulbs, plugs and fuses; clearing blockages in sinks and basins caused by misuse; fences between your garden and a neighbour's, unless the fence was installed by us in the last 5 years; and any gas appliance you own yourself, such as a gas cooker you bought. You must arrange for your own gas appliances to be installed and serviced by a Gas Safe registered engineer.

5. Lock-outs and lost keys. If you are locked out or lose your keys, we will attend and change the locks free of charge only if you give us a police crime reference number showing that the keys were stolen. In all other cases a charge of £65 will be made, payable before the work is done, or you may call a locksmith yourself.

6. Access. You must allow access for repairs and safety checks at reasonable times. We will give at least 24 hours' notice except in an emergency. If you miss two appointments without letting us know, we may close the repair request.

7. Missed appointments by us. If we fail to attend an agreed appointment without giving you at least 24 hours' notice, we will pay you £15 compensation, credited to your rent account.

8. Damage by tenants. Where damage has been caused deliberately or through neglect by a tenant, household member or visitor, we will recharge the full cost of the repair.

9. Assisted repairs. Tenants aged 75 or over, or with a disability, and with no one in the household able to help, may ask us to carry out minor tenant-responsibility jobs such as replacing light bulbs or toilet seats.

10. Complaints. If you are unhappy with a repair, you can use our complaints procedure and, after that, the Housing Ombudsman.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. How quickly will someone attend an emergency repair like a gas leak?
2. I reported a dripping kitchen tap 15 working days ago and it hasn't been fixed yet. Is Tamar Valley outside its target time?
3. The gas cooker I bought myself needs a safety check. Will Tamar Valley do it at the annual gas check?
4. I dropped my keys in the river — they weren't stolen. Will the locks be changed for free?
response:
Answers are taken from the policy document itself. Several of my earlier notes were wrong, and I've marked where.

**1. Emergency repairs (e.g. a gas leak):** Someone will attend within **4 hours**, and the problem will be made safe within **24 hours**. A follow-on repair may be needed afterwards. Emergencies must be **reported by telephone** on 0345 600 2210, not online or by email.

**2. Dripping tap after 15 working days:** **No, they are not yet outside the target.** A dripping tap is a routine repair, and the target for routine repairs is **20 working days** (section 2). You have 5 working days left. *(My notes wrongly said 10 working days.)* If it isn't fixed after 20 working days, you can use the complaints procedure (section 10).

**3. Gas cooker you bought yourself:** **No.** The annual gas safety check only covers appliances Tamar Valley **installed**, such as boilers and fires (section 3). A cooker you own is your responsibility. You must arrange for it to be serviced by a **Gas Safe registered engineer** (section 4). *(My notes wrongly said all gas appliances, including cookers, were covered.)*

**4. Keys lost in the river:** **No, it won't be free.** Locks are changed free only if you give a **police crime reference number** showing the keys were stolen. Otherwise there is a **£65 charge, payable before the work is done**, or you can call a locksmith yourself (section 5). *(My notes wrongly said lock changes were always free.)*
